caption: A layer of white sugar in a dry pan over heat melts from the edges into a clear liquid that turns amber and then deep brown.

sa.check: A layer of white sugar lies in a dry pan over heat.
The sugar melts from the edges inward.
The melt is a clear liquid.
The liquid darkens to amber and then deep brown.
Thin smoke may rise at the end.
The melting comes first and the darkening follows.

pc.expect: The melting only advances inward from the edges and the darkening only deepens; neither reverses.
pc.fail: A melted part turns back into white grains; or the melting spreads and then retreats; or the dark liquid lightens back to amber or clear; or the sugar melts at the centre first and works out to the edges.

pc.expect: The colour change happens in the liquid itself and runs one way from clear to amber to brown.
pc.fail: The pan's surface changes colour rather than the sugar; or the liquid is brown before any sugar has melted; or the liquid's colour goes back and forth between amber and brown; or the dry grains turn brown while still unmelted.

pc.expect: The melted sugar runs to the pan's low places and spreads across its floor, and any smoke rises.
pc.fail: The melt climbs the pan's wall and stays; or a run travels uphill; or melted sugar lifts off the pan; or the smoke sinks over the rim and pools on the hob.

pc.expect: The sugar goes from loose dry grains to a thick glossy liquid that flows slowly and levels.
pc.fail: The melt runs as thin as water; or the grains stay dry and separate while the layer flows; or the melt sets solid in the hot pan; or the liquid stands as a rigid dome.

pc.expect: The sugar in the pan is the sugar that was there; it melts rather than appearing or vanishing.
pc.fail: Sugar appears in the pan with none added; or the layer vanishes at a stroke; or a second pan appears; or the melt passes through the pan's floor.

pc.expect: The pan's finish, the hob and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The pan changes colour; or its handle changes shape; or items around the hob rearrange.

note: The sugar's browning is the caption's asserted outcome; the chemistry of it is not judged, only that the colour runs one way and the melting starts at the edges.
